deliverables: Periodic independent audits of treasury fund use and oversight metrics
Eternl Pro plan rollout and related repayment reporting
request.what: Treasury withdrawal to fund 12 months of Eternl operations, maintenance, and improvements, including frontend and backend work, infrastructure, support, administration, and audits/oversight.

claims.claim: Eternl requests ₳2,350,000, valued at about $0.1787 per Ada, to cover approximately $420,000 in annual costs for a 12-month operating period.
The proposal funds 6.0 FTE distributed across 10 contributors at $70,000 per FTE.
Eternl states it has about 100,000 browser extension installs and about 30,000 Android and iOS installs.
The proposer claims that if about 4.2% of the install base, or roughly 5,500 users, buy the Pro plan, Pro income alone would fully cover the annual $420,000 cost.
The proposer commits to convert up to $420,000 worth of Ada into stablecoins, deposit it into a public company wallet, and return any Ada above that amount to the treasury.

The proposer commits to assess repayment every December and June and use surplus treasury stablecoins plus paid plan income above $420,000 to repay the treasury until $420,000 in Ada value has been repaid.

The proposer states an unaffiliated independent party will audit treasury fund use in February 2027 and August 2027, reviewing custody, conversion, spending, balances, Pro plan income relevant to repayment, and refunds or repayments.
Eternl claims 10-18% of Cardano mainnet transactions are conducted via Eternl.
Eternl states its main UI will not be open-source, while some libraries used by Eternl will be published through the npm registry.

The proposer states that without enough funding or paid license sales beyond August, it may let developers go, scale Eternl down to essential maintenance, shift focus outside Cardano, or remove the free option.

summary: The document requests ₳2,350,000 for one year of Eternl operations and proposes a paid Pro plan, public wallet custody, independent fund-use audits, and conditional treasury repayment, but many adoption, feasibility, and risk claims are asserted without detailed supporting evidence.
